questions.question: In a food chain, _______ can be taken as the average value for the amount of organic matter that is present at each step and reaches the next level of consumers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10%.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term "**trophic level transfer efficiency**" is the average amount of organic matter that is transferred from one trophic level to the next.
 
• This value is usually around **10%,** meaning that only 10% of the organic matter from one level is transferred to the next level.
 
• Because** energy is lost** as metabolic heat when animals from one trophic level are consumed by species from the next,** energy declines** as it goes up the trophic levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **food chain** is a straight line made up of creatures in which **energy and nutrients** are passed from one to the next.
 
• When one creature **eats** another, this happens. 
 
• The **decomposer** organism comes at the end of the chain, having started with the producer **organism. **

questions.question: Who has been appointed as the second Chief of Defence Staff of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lieutenant General Anil Chauhan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anil Chauhan** is an** Indian Army general** with four stars.
 
• Since **September 30, 2022**, he has served as the Indian Armed Forces' **second Chief of Defence Staff** (CDS).
 
• The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) is a **four-star general rank **officer who serves as the principal military advisor to the government of India.
 
• The CDS is responsible for ensuring jointness and integration among the three services -** Army, Navy, and Air Force** - in terms of operations, logistics, training, and procurement.
 
• The CDS was created as a new position in the Indian armed forces in** 2019**, and **General Bipin Rawat **became the first CDS.
 
• The appointment of the CDS is a significant step towards achieving **greater synergy and coordination** among the Indian armed forces, and it is expected to enhance India's national security and defence preparedness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **General Manoj Mukund Naravane** is the current **Chief of Army Staff **(COAS) of the Indian Army.

 
 
• He assumed office on **31 December 2019.**
 
 
 
• Lieutenant General **Baggavalli Somashekar Raju** is a serving officer in the Indian Army.
 
 
• He is currently the** General Officer Commanding-in-Chief **(GOC-in-C) of the Army Training Command (ARTRAC) in Shimla.

questions.question: When a national GST subsumed central taxes on July 1, 2017, how many petroleum goods were kept out of its purview for the time being?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Five.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Five petroleum goods** were kept out of the purview of GST for the time being.
 
• The five petroleum goods that were excluded from the GST are **crude oil, natural gas, aviation turbine fuel, diesel, and petrol.**
 
• The reason for keeping these petroleum goods outside the purview of GST is that they generate a significant amount of **revenue** for both the central and state governments, and bringing them under GST would have led to a **substantial loss** in revenue.
 
• The exclusion of petroleum goods from GST has been a subject of debate and criticism, as it leads to **cascading taxes** and** increases the final price** of these goods.
 
• The government has been considering bringing **petroleum goods** under GST, but it has not yet made any concrete decisions in this regard.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GST** stands for Goods and Services Tax, which is a comprehensive **indirect tax levied** on the supply of **goods and services** in India.
 
• The GST was implemented on **July 1, 2017,** and it replaced multiple indirect taxes that were levied by both the **central and state** governments.
 
• For the purpose of collecting taxes, goods and services are separated into five tax slabs: **0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%**.
 
• But under the **old tax structure, alcohol, petroleum products, and electricity** were all subject to separate state-level taxes rather than being taxable under the GST.

questions.question: Fa Xian began his journey back from _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengal**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fa Xian** was a **Chinese Buddhist monk** who traveled to India to study **Buddhism** and collect **Buddhist texts.**
 
• Fa-Hien's book **Fo-kwo-ki **contains writings about India.
 
• He spoke of the **Mahayana and Hinayana** monasteries in Pataliputra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fa Xian** traveled to India during the reign of **Emperor Chandragupta II** (375-415 CE).
 
• He spent several years in India, visiting important **Buddhist sites **and studying Buddhist texts.
 
• Fa Xian's journey to India is considered one of the earliest and most important accounts of **Buddhist pilgrimage **to India.
 
• Patliputra (present-day Patna) was an important city in ancient India and was known for its** rich culture and learning.**
 
• It was the **capital** of the **Mauryan Empire **and later the Gupta Empire.

questions.question: Vishu is a _______ festival, celebrated primarily in the southern part of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindu.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vishu** is primarily celebrated in the southern Indian state of **Kerala** and marks the beginning of the **Malayalam New Year.**
 
• It is a **Hindu** festival.
 
• The festival is celebrated on the first day of the **Malayalam month of Medam** which usually falls in the month of **April.**
 
• The festival is celebrated with **great enthusiasm** and involves various rituals such as **Vishukkani, Vishukkaineetam, and Vishu Sadya.**
 
• The festival is also considered as a **harvest festival **and people offer prayers to the deity for a prosperous harvest season.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buddhist festivals** are celebrated by followers of Buddhism and are primarily observed in countries where Buddhism is the major religion such as **Thailand, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, **etc.

 
 
• Some of the popular Buddhist festivals include **Vesak, Magha Puja, Asalha Puja**, etc.
 
 
 
• **Parsi festivals** are celebrated by followers of **Zoroastrianism** and are primarily observed in **Iran and India.**
 
 
• Some of the popular Parsi festivals include **Navroz, Khordad Sal, Mehregan**, etc.
 
 
 
• **Jain festivals** are celebrated by followers of** Jainism** and are primarily observed in India.
 
 
• Some of the popular Jain festivals include **Mahavir Jayanti, Paryushan Parva, Diwali,** etc.

questions.question: There were two Annual Programs implemented in India in 1990-91 and 1991-92 (between _______ five year plans).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**seventh and eighth.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Two Annual Programs** were implemented in India in **1990-91 and 1991-92.**
 
• These programs were implemented between the** seventh and eighth** five year plans.
 
• The main objective of these programs was to increase **agricultural productivity** and** rural development.**
 
• The programs aimed to provide support to farmers and improve **infrastructure** in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Indian economy** was built on the idea of planning from **1947 until 2017.**
 
• This was implemented through the Five-Year Plans, which were created, carried out, and overseen by the **NITI Aayog **and the** Planning Commission. **
 
• **First and second five year plans** were implemented much earlier, between **1951-1956** and **1956-1961 **respectively.
 
• **Third and fourth** five year plans were implemented between** 1961-1966 **and **1969-1974** respectively.
 
• **Fifth and sixth **five year plans were implemented between **1974-1979** and **1980-1985** respectively.

questions.question: In India, the 'Green Revolution' mainly started in the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1960's.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Green Revolution** refers to a period of significant **agricultural development** that took place in India during the **1960s and 1970s.**
 
• The main objective of the Green Revolution was to increase agricultural production and productivity by introducing new technologies, high-yielding varieties of **seeds, **and** modern farming practices.**
 
• The Green Revolution played a crucial role in making India **self-sufficient** in food production and reducing its dependence on food imports.
 
• The Green Revolution also led to the emergence of a new class of** wealthy farmers**, who were able to take advantage of the new technologies and farming practices to increase their **income and standard of living.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Norman Borlaug** launched the Green Revolution initiative in the **1960s.**
 
• He is regarded globally as the** "Father of the Green Revolution."**
 
• As a result, he was awarded the **Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 **for his contributions to the creation of **wheat High Yielding Varieties** (HYVs).

questions.question: Which of the following is caused by Loo?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heat Stroke.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Loo** is a term used in **India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh **to describe a **hot, dry, and dusty **wind that blows during the summer season.
 
• Loo is known to cause various health problems, including **dehydration, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke.**
 
• The most **dangerou**s heat-related ailment is heat stroke.
 
• It happens when the** body loses the ability** to regulate its temperature.
 
• The body temperature might increase to** 106°F** or more in** 10 to 15 minutes** when heat stroke strikes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hypothermia** is a condition that occurs when the body temperature drops below normal levels.

 
 
• It is caused due to exposure to **cold temperatures. **
 
 
 
• **Frostbite** is a condition that occurs when the **skin** and underlying **tissues freeze.**
 
 
• It is caused due to exposure to extreme **cold temperatures.**
 
 
 
• **Chilblains** are **small, itchy, and painful red bumps** that develop on the skin.
 
 
• It occurs due to exposure to **cold and damp** conditions.

questions.question:
Parliament consists of _______.

(i) President

(ii) The Council of States

(iii) The House of the People
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i), (ii) and (iii).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parliament **is the supreme legislative body of India, which consists of the **President **and the two Houses, i.e., the **Council of States **(Rajya Sabha) and the **House of the People** (Lok Sabha).
 
• The President is **not **a member of Parliament but an** integral part** of it as he/she **summons and prorogues **the sessions of Parliament and gives assent to the bills passed by both the Houses.
 
• The **Council of States** (Rajya Sabha) is also known as the Upper House of Parliament, which represents the states and union territories of India.
 
 
• It has a total of **245 members**, out of which 233 are elected by the members of the Legislative Assemblies of the states and union territories, and** 12** are nominated by the President.
 
 
 
• The **House of the People** (Lok Sabha) is also known as the Lower House of Parliament, which represents the people of India.
 
 
• It has a total of **545 members.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
 

 
• In** New Delhi, **the Parliament convenes at **Sansad Bhavan.**
 
• With **912 million **eligible voters in** 2019**, the Indian Parliament represents the largest **democratic electorate** in the world (the European Parliament comes in second).
 
• A **bill** is the document that **legislative proposals** are presented in front of either chamber of parliament. 
 
• A bill is a draft legislative proposal that becomes an **act of Parliament **after it is approved by both chambers and the president.

questions.question: Which schedule of Indian constitution contains languages of Republic of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 8.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Constitution recognizes **22 languages** and **Schedule 8** lists these languages.
 
• These include **Hindi, English, Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu**, and others.
 
• **Schedule 8 **also mentions the official languages of different states in India.
 
• For example**, Assamese** is the official language of Assam, **Kannada **is the official language of Karnataka, and so on.
 
• The Constitution also provides for the **promotion and development** of these languages.
 
• For instance, **Article 350A** mandates that every state should provide facilities for instruction in the **mother-tongue **at the primary stage of education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Schedule 7 **of the Indian Constitution deals with the **Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. **
 
• **Schedule 9** of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions for the **administration of tribal areas** in India. 
 
• **Schedule 6** of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration of certain **tribal areas in northeastern **India.
 
• The Indian Constitution consists of **12 Schedules**.
 
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935,** which contained 10 Schedules, was one of the earliest documents to mention schedules.
 
• Eight Schedules made up the Indian Constitution when it was eventually enacted in **1949.**

questions.question: What happens in plantation farming?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**single crop is grown.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plantation farming** is a type of **commercial agriculture** where crops are grown on a** large scale** for profit.
 
• In plantation farming, a** single crop is grown** over a large area, usually in a **monoculture system.**
 
• This means that the **same crop** is grown repeatedly on the same land.
 
• The crops grown in plantation farming are usually cash crops, such as** tea, coffee, rubber, cotton, sugarcane, and palm oil.**
 
• These crops are in high demand and are used for **export** or for domestic consumption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plantation farming** requires specialized** knowledge, labor, and equipment** to maintain the crops and ensure their productivity.

 
 
• The use of **pesticides, fertilizers, and irrigation systems** is common in plantation farming.
 
• Plantation farming has been criticized for its** negative environmental and social impacts**, such as deforestation, soil degradation, water pollution, and exploitation of workers.
 
 
 
• Some forms of **agroforestry or mixed cropping** may involve growing multiple crops in the same field, which can have** ecological and economic** benefits.
 
• Some plantations may specialize in **two crops** that complement each other, such as **coffee and cocoa,** or sugarcane and ethanol.
 
• Some plantations may adopt **intercropping **or cover cropping techniques to improve **soil fertility **and reduce pest and disease pressure.

questions.question: There are _______ hand gestures in Mohiniyattam which are mainly adopted from Hastalakshana Deepika text.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mohiniyattam is literally interpreted as the dance of ‘***Mohini***’.
 
• It is one of the two classical dance forms that originated in Kerala, the other one being Kathakali.
 
• It contains **24 **hand gestures in Mohiniyattam which are mainly adopted from Hastalakshana Deepika text.
 
• It is based on **Natya Shastra’s lasya style.**
 
• It has delicate movements and more **feminine facial** expressions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The repertoire of Mohiniyattam includes music in the **Carnatic style,** singing and acting a play through the dance, where the recitation may be either by a **separate vocalist **or the dancer themselves.
 
• The song is typically in Malayalam-Sanskrit hybrid called **Manipravalam**
 
• The movements are **gentle and glide-like.**
 
• They do **not** have terse rhythmic steps.
 
• More emphasis is on the** facial expressions **and** hand gestures.**

questions.question: Milkha Singh, the Flying Sikh, was the first Indian to win a gold medal in which of the following games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Commonwealth Games.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Milkha Singh**, also known as the **Flying Sikh**, won a **gold medal** in the **400m race** at the **Commonwealth Games** held in **Cardiff in 1958.**
 
• In the Asian Games in **1958 and 1962,** he also took home gold medals. 
 
• For his athletic accomplishments, he was given the** Padma Shri, **the fourth-highest civilian honor in India.
 
• Singh was referred to as "**the finest athlete India has ever produced"** by columnist Rohit Brijnath in** 2008.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cardiff, Wales **hosted the **1958 British Empire** and **Commonwealth Games** from **July 18–26.**
 
• A total of 1,130 competitors and 228 officials were sent by **35 nations** to the Cardiff Games.
 
• The **Queen's Baton Relay** was also inaugurated during the 1958 event.
 
• On the first leg of the Queen's Baton's voyage to Wales, two of England's most renowned middle distance runners,** Roger Bannister and Chris Chattaway,** were given the honor of accepting it at **Buckingham Palace.**

questions.question: The Logo of 36th National Games of India contains a Picture of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lion.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **36th National Games of India **were scheduled to be held in **Goa in 2020** but were postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• The logo of the National Games of India features a **blue and orange lion **with the number **36** written in bold letters.
 
• Lions are often associated with **strength, power, and courage**, making them a fitting symbol for a national sporting event.
 
• The use of a lion in the logo also represents India's rich cultural heritage, as the animal has significant** symbolism **in Hindu mythology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **37th National Games of India** are another name for the **2023** edition of the competition.
 
• They took place in the state of **Goa** from October 25, 2023, to November 9, 2023.
 
• In June 2023, the games' official logo and mascot, an** Indian bison named Moga**, were announced.
 
• The** Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy, **which is given to the team with the most gold medals at the National Games, was won by **Maharashtra,** who also led the medal count in the 2023 National Games.

questions.question: Constitutional requirement to present the Annual Financial Statement before parliament is given in article _______ of the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**112.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 112** of the Constitution of India deals with the** annual financial **statement, also known as the **Union Budget**.
 
• It states that the **President** shall, at the beginning of every financial year, lay before Parliament the annual financial statement for the year.
 
• The annual financial statement includes the** estimated receipts and expenditure** of the government for the upcoming financial year and is prepared by the **Ministry of Finance.**
 
• The statement is presented in the form of a budget, which is discussed and approved by **both the houses of Parliament** before it comes into effect.
 
• The Constitution of India also mandates that the budget should distinguish between expenditure charged upon the** Consolidated Fund of India **and other expenditure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 12 **of the Constitution deals with the **definition of the State.**
 
• **Article 121** deals with the** restriction** on discussion in Parliament.
 
• **Article 123 **deals with the **power of the President **to promulgate ordinances.
 
• The** Constitution of India** is the supreme law of the country and lays down the framework for the** governance of India.**
 
• It was adopted on** 26th November 1949** and came into effect on** 26th January 1950**, marking the beginning of a new era in the history of India.
 
• The Constitution has **448 articles** in** 25 parts **and **12 schedules**, making it one of the **lengthiest written constitutions** in the world.
 
• It provides for a **federal system of government **with a division of powers between the central and state governments.
 
• The Constitution also guarantees** fundamental rights** to all citizens and outlines the duties of the government towards them.
